title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 199
paragraphs: Moreover, the territory of Cyrene, which is the highest part of Libya occupied by nomads, contains within its borders three seasons of harvest, at which we may well marvel. First the parts along the sea-coast have their fruit ripe for reaping and grapes ready for the vintage; and when these have been gathered in, the parts lying above the coastal region, in the middle—what they call the hills—are ready to be gathered in; and as soon as this middle crop is gathered, the crop in the highest part of the country comes to perfection and is ripe. So by the time the first crop has been eaten and drunk up, the last is just coming in. In this way the harvest for the Cyrenaeans lasts eight months. So much for these matters.
